title: Anthropic asks candidates about shares falling to zero
content:
Anthropic asks candidates about shares falling to zero — Fortune
Anthropic, which is headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area in the United States, asks candidates during interviews about corporate culture how they would feel about a scenario in which the company abandons its AI ambitions for safety reasons and its shares fall to zero. Fortune reports, citing Axios.
One candidate who described the hiring process on Blind, an anonymous website for employees, said that they would not be happy if the shares fell to zero. At the same time, they said they would like to combine ethical work and benefits with building a financially sustainable business.
Possible IPO
According to Fortune, Anthropic is targeting an IPO in November with a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion. The company has more than 2,500 employees, and going public at such a valuation could potentially make some staff millionaires thanks to their stakes in the company.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, according to the publication, has expressed concern about how significant financial incentives could affect the company's ability to retain employees committed to its mission. Anthropic is a public benefit corporation and emphasizes AI safety and the long-term benefit of technology for humanity.
More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.
Competition for specialists
The company competes for researchers and engineers with Meta, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI. In an S-1 document dated October 26, Anthropic said that competition for qualified employees, especially in the San Francisco Bay Area, has intensified significantly.
Base salaries for staff software engineer positions at Anthropic range from $350,000 to $850,000 a year, Fortune writes. The company also has more than 600 open positions, including about 120 in sales, more than 60 in AI research and engineering, and 50 in safety.
Amodei previously warned that the economic benefits of AI could be concentrated among a limited circle of people. He and six other Anthropic co-founders, including his sister Daniela Amodei, pledged to give away 80% of their wealth.

report.summary: Anthropic reportedly asks job candidates how they would react if safety-driven decisions made its shares worthless, spotlighting mission-versus-equity tensions before a possible IPO.
report.background: Anthropic, founded by former OpenAI researchers, positions itself as an AI safety-focused public benefit corporation. It competes with Meta, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI for scarce AI researchers and engineers, especially in the San Francisco Bay Area. According to Fortune, citing Axios, Anthropic uses interview questions to test whether candidates align with its mission, including a hypothetical in which the company abandons AI ambitions for safety reasons and its shares fall to zero. The question lands as Anthropic reportedly targets a very high-value IPO, which could create significant wealth for employees with equity. CEO Dario Amodei has reportedly worried that financial incentives could complicate retention of staff committed to the mission. The story reflects broader tension in frontier AI: safety-oriented governance, rapid commercialization, and intense talent competition.
key_points: Anthropic reportedly asks candidates a hypothetical: if the company abandoned AI ambitions for safety and shares fell to zero, how would they feel? The question probes mission alignment and cultural fit, not just technical skill.
One candidate told Blind they would not be happy with zero-value shares but wanted to combine ethical work with a financially sustainable business, illustrating the tension candidates face.
Fortune reports Anthropic is targeting a November IPO at a $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion valuation. With more than 2,500 employees, equity could make some staff millionaires.
CEO Dario Amodei has reportedly expressed concern that large financial incentives could affect Anthropic’s ability to retain employees committed to its safety mission.

Anthropic competes for talent with major AI firms. Reported base salaries for staff software engineers range from $350,000 to $850,000, and the company has more than 600 open roles, including safety and research positions.
report.impact: The report signals that mission-driven AI labs are testing candidates for values as equity becomes potentially life-changing. For the AI industry, it highlights a governance challenge: safety commitments can conflict with financial incentives, especially near an IPO. For developers and researchers, it adds a new interview dimension—willingness to accept mission risk alongside compensation risk. For regular users, the credibility of safety-first claims depends on whether companies can retain mission-committed staff when wealth and growth pressures intensify. If financial incentives dominate, public trust in AI safety governance could weaken; if handled well, it could set a precedent for aligning talent, equity, and responsible AI development.
report.tools: No dedicated open-source tool is tied to this story. To follow up, read Anthropic’s Responsible Scaling Policy and public benefit corporation charter; monitor SEC EDGAR for S-1 and IPO filings; use Levels.fyi for compensation comparisons; follow Fortune, Axios, and Blind for hiring-culture discussion; and track Anthropic’s careers page for safety and research roles.
